original_card.question: Can a new local cost interface change the deficit-to-recursive-cost ratio beyond current packing?
methods: Propose a changed helper inventory and derive an optimistic exact moment.
Design a small completed instance and independently verify its endpoint and rank bill.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A new physically realizable contract outside the frozen catalogue whose per-call profile, screened with ceiling.ceiling(), beats the selected word's packing ceiling; a lower cap does not establish identical circuitry or order attainable optima, and is insufficient to pass the stronger-budget target under this model.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Packing of the selected word is capped at +0.87% (ceiling model); only a lower local excess spend or a changed coverage law raises the cap.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one changed boundary or helper type with explicit counts.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Mixing only providers already inside the pinned catalogue.

actual_scope: Price the E8 port-count / puncture-depth lever (V = 120 - p, attained eight-term decoder floor cst = max(72 - p, 56), p <= 24) with #1240's exact packing ceiling, using PR717's per-port knob on the selected #1094 local word (plus a proportional-scaling sensitivity). Report the argmax, one-lever marginals, per-port excess versus budget, sharp break-even decoder constants per V for three targets, and whether any V <= 120 reaches a = 1/99.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a new physically realizable helper interface. This session instead answers #1240's open question on how the target budget scales with port count, which is a screening budget for the decoder/puncture line of work (many open P104/P111/82-port decoder PRs rank by cst/v). No interface or word is constructed, so the card's acceptance gate is not met.
bottleneck_link: The complex side binds. Port count and decoder constant enter the deficit directly (D = 8V/9 - cst per call). This package shows that on the attained E8 floor the combined lever is capped at x1.054 of the selected word's ceiling (enough only to unbind, never 1/99), and that cst/v is not the moment-relevant figure of merit.
stop_rule: Stop after the floor chain p = 0..24, the 82-port witnesses, the break-even table on V in {82, 96..120} and one sensitivity model. No word synthesis.
evidence: RESULT.json: P104 ceiling a < 0.001781965481 (x1.05438, kappa < 0.0017788) is the chain argmax in both models; a port's excess is below its budget increment even at 1/99, but 1/99 needs V >= 1328 at cst 64; break-even cst table; cst/V counterexample P112 vs P98; 22 checks.
author: Jack Galler
ai_assistance: Substantial: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic, Claude Code) chose the model, wrote verify.py and drafted the README; the account holder directed the session.

open_questions.question: What is the actual per-call local profile of a P104 word built like #1094?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The knob model is marginal; P104 is the largest attained-floor headroom (x1.054 knob, x1.10 proportional) and decides whether this lever can unbind the complex side.
open_questions.first_step: Build the P104 analogue of the selected local word and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(local, 73, 832, 9, 56).
open_questions.blocked_by: Asymmetric-centre realization (PR717 unpaired-centre parity costs and pair-split conflicts).

open_questions.question: Do the larger-alphabet unit screens (#620 ade_screen, #895 BW16) survive re-pricing with the #1240 ceiling and a per-port knob?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Per-port excess is below the per-port budget even at a = 1/99, so V is the one non-saturating lever, but E8 caps V at 120 (1/99 would need V >= 1328 at cst 64); those screens rank units by the ratio proxy x = c*h/v, which this package shows can misorder words with a V-independent part.
open_questions.first_step: Write one larger unit's coverage law, centre floor and per-port knob and price it with this verifier's word() and max_cst().
open_questions.blocked_by: A per-port knob and an attained centre floor for that unit.
